thread:
Jamie: Quick sync — we need a concise scope for JSON-mode launch. Customer asks and launch criteria are getting fuzzy. Can we align on what 'validation + retry' actually means for GA?
Leo (eng-runtime): For me it's two axes: enforcement mode (soft vs hard) and retry policy (automatic vs suggested). Soft = attach validation errors but return original text; Hard = block and return structured error.
Maria (eng-ml): Also need to decide whether we run schema validation pre-tokenization (cheap) or post-generation (accurate). Pre-tokenization validation is only possible for tool inputs; real generated JSON must be validated after decode.
Ashley (devex): From DX we should expose a single flag: json_mode: { "enforcement": "soft|hard|repair", "retry": "auto|manual", "schema": "url|inline" }. Keep defaults conservative.
Sylvia (customer-success): Customers asking for deterministic contracts. Enterprise wants hard enforcement + automatic retry with canary behavior. But smaller teams prefer soft + hints.
Jamie: Good. Proposal: GA default = soft enforcement + no automatic retry. Enterprise + paid tiers unlock hard enforcement + auto-retry with fallback variants. Thoughts?
Leo (eng-runtime): Sounds safe. Two engineering constraints: auto-retry must not exceed latency SLOs and must respect prefix caching (don't re-run previously cached tokens). We should allow 'max_retry_attempts' and 'total_retry_token_budget'.
Maria: For auto-repair option we can run a lightweight edit model (small finetune or instruction-following) to try to fix schema violations before a full retry. That reduces cost vs a full re-gen. Label it 'repair' enforcement.
Ashley (devex): UX: show validation details in the response metadata so app can choose to ignore. For hard enforcement, include a machine-friendly error code and a suggested patch snippet. E.g. response.metadata.validation = { valid: false, errors: [...], suggested_fix: "{...}" }
Leo (eng-runtime): Implementation note: we'll implement validation as a pluggable stage after decode. For retries we can support two modes: client-visible retry (server returns suggestion + client calls /completions with patch) or server-side transparent retry (server retries and returns final structured JSON). Need opt-in for transparent retries.
Jamie: Launch criteria checklist draft: 1) Schema spec support (refs + $ref local) 2) Validation post-decode with detailed error codes 3) Soft enforcement default with metadata 4) Hard enforcement + transparent retry behind enterprise flag 5) Repair pipeline (best-effort) 6) Test corpus and evals for top 20 customer schemas 7) Docs + SDK helpers + sample prompts
Sylvia: Add success metric: percent of responses that pass schema on first attempt (baseline target 80% for GA on curated models). Also time-to-repair for auto-repair path.
Maria: Need to pick models for repair path. Small instruction models (<=7B quantized) for edit proposals then full model if we escalate. Also track hallucination rate post-repair.
Ashley: SDKs: provide a helper that wraps retries with exponential backoff and token budget awareness. Example snippet in JS: ```js
const out = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'redwood-available',
  json_mode: { enforcement: 'hard', retry: 'auto', max_retry_attempts: 2 },
  prompt: 'Generate invoice JSON schema...'
})
```
Leo (eng-runtime): Operational limits: default max_retry_attempts=1, total_retry_token_budget=2048 tokens. Also require explicit consent for transparent retries in privacy-sensitive accounts (Private deployment).
Jamie: Risk points to document: - user app logic that relies on best-effort JSON may break if we flip to hard enforcement later. Need migration guide. - cost impact of retries for high-throughput workloads. - failure modes where repair makes things worse.
Sylvia: Customer-facing messaging: "JSON mode helps enforce structured outputs. Defaults are conservative; enterprise options for stricter enforcement and automated correction."
Ashley: Action items: 1) Eng to spec API flags and server-side behavior (Leo/Maria) 2) Devex to draft SDK helpers + migration guide (Ashley) 3) Product to assemble GA eval set and customer comms (Jamie/Sylvia) 4) Security/privacy check for transparent server retries (ops-bot will create ticket).
ops-bot: Ticket created: INF-PRIV-4123 for privacy review of server-side transparent retries.
Leo (eng-runtime): I'll put up a short RFC by EOW describing validation pipeline, retry budget, and telemetry.
Maria: I'll prototype the repair pipeline with a small model and share numbers (latency/cost/accuracy).
Jamie: Great. Let's reconvene after RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
